title: CoopMatch Studio
concept:
=== APPROVED PRODUCT BRIEF (the user picked this from a 5-brief set; build EXACTLY this) ===

Frame: convention-honoring (probability 0.4)
Title: CoopMatch Studio
Thesis: A skill-matching dashboard pairing Northeastern students with co-op employers via competency profiles and explained placement-fit predictions.
Why this frame: This is the schema-congruent build any competent ed-tech designer would ship: a two-sided marketplace with AI matching mirroring LinkedIn-meets-Handshake conventions familiar to career services. It honors expectations while making fit reasoning legible.

PRIMARY PERSONA:
  Name: Maya Chen
  Role: Third-year Behavioral Neuroscience major preparing for first co-op cycle
  Context: Northeastern's spring co-op cycle. Maya has solid coursework but no industry experience, a half-finished resume, and a vague sense that her lab skills might translate to UX research or clinical roles but no proof.
  Emotional state: Anxious and slightly paralyzed — afraid she'll waste applications on roles that auto-reject her, comparing herself to peers who seem 'ahead.'
  Pain points:
    - Cannot tell which of her skills employers actually weight, so she over-applies blindly
    - Generic job boards surface hundreds of postings with no sense of realistic fit
    - Rewriting her resume for each role is exhausting and she doesn't know what to emphasize
    - No clear signal on what single skill would meaningfully expand her opportunity set
  JTBD: When I start my co-op search, I want to see which employers realistically fit my actual competencies and why, so I can apply with confidence to roles I can land and grow from.
SECONDARY ACTORS:
  - Co-op Employer Recruiter: Posts roles with required competencies, reviews matched candidates, schedules interviews, sends placement offers
  - Northeastern Co-op Faculty Coordinator: Reviews student readiness, approves placements, monitors cohort outcomes, intervenes on low-match students
  - Peer Student in same cohort: Provides social benchmarking signal and optional skill-endorsement; appears anonymized in aggregate readiness comparisons
  - Alumni Mentor: Surfaced for roles where they previously co-oped; offers async prep tips referenced in skill-gap plans

DEMONSTRATED MOMENT: Maya completes her competency profile and watches a ranked, color-coded list of co-op matches assemble itself — each with a plain-language fit rationale — then sees a callout: 'Add Python basics → unlocks 5 more roles.'

USE CASES (12) - the prototype MUST demonstrate at least 5 of these as live flows:
  1. Build competency profile
     Trigger: Maya logs in for the first time and is greeted by a guided skills intake that pre-fills from her transcript and resume upload.
     Flow: Maya uploads her resume and connects her transcript → the system extracts candidate competencies and asks her to confirm or adjust proficiency on each → she rates 12 surfaced skills on a 4-level scale → she tags 3 interest areas → profile completeness meter fills to 100%.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro parses resume and transcript into a structured competency taxonomy, infers proficiency levels, and proposes skills Maya forgot to list based on her coursework.
     Outcome: Maya has a verified competency profile with 18 tagged skills and proficiency levels, ready for matching, in under 8 minutes.
  2. Discover ranked co-op matches
     Trigger: Profile completion triggers the match feed to populate automatically.
     Flow: Maya lands on the match feed → 40+ open co-op roles are scored and sorted by fit → top matches show a green/amber/red fit band → she filters by location, pay, and industry → she saves 6 roles to a shortlist.
     AI role: Fit-scoring model computes a 0–100 placement-fit score per role from competency overlap, proficiency depth, and historical placement patterns for similar students.
     Outcome: Maya sees a curated, ranked shortlist instead of an undifferentiated wall of postings, focusing her energy on winnable roles.
  3. Understand match-fit rationale
     Trigger: Maya taps a specific role card to open its detail view.
     Flow: She opens the match detail → reads a 3-bullet rationale of why she fits → sees a competency-match radar comparing her profile to role requirements → notes which 2 skills are 'partial' → reads what would close each gap.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 generates plain-language, encouraging rationale explaining the numeric score, grounded in the specific competency overlaps and gaps.
     Outcome: Maya understands precisely why the role is a 78% fit and exactly what separates her from a 90%, removing the black-box anxiety.
  4. Apply with auto-tailored materials
     Trigger: Maya clicks 'Apply' on a shortlisted role.
     Flow: She clicks Apply → the assistant drafts a tailored resume variant and cover letter emphasizing role-relevant competencies → she reviews tracked-change suggestions → she accepts/edits → she submits in one click.
     AI role: Claude Opus 4.7 rewrites resume bullet emphasis and drafts a cover letter anchored to the role's required competencies and Maya's verified strengths.
     Outcome: Maya submits a genuinely tailored application in 3 minutes instead of 45, with confidence the emphasis is right.
  5. Track application pipeline status
     Trigger: Maya returns after submitting several applications to check progress.
     Flow: She opens the tracker board → sees columns Applied / Viewed / Interviewing / Offer → cards move automatically as employers act → she sees time-in-stage and nudges for stale applications → she archives rejections.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro summarizes pipeline health and flags applications likely to stall, suggesting follow-up timing.
     Outcome: Maya has a single calm view of her entire search with zero spreadsheet maintenance.
  6. Schedule employer interviews
     Trigger: A recruiter advances Maya to the interview stage.
     Flow: She gets a notification → opens the scheduler → sees recruiter's offered slots overlaid with her class calendar → picks a conflict-free slot → confirms → gets a prep checklist for that role.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro detects calendar conflicts and recommends optimal slots accounting for travel and prep buffer.
     Outcome: Maya books interviews without email tag and arrives prepared, reducing scheduling friction to two taps.
  7. Receive pre-placement skill prep
     Trigger: A role becomes a strong match but shows a closable skill gap.
     Flow: She opens the skill-gap prep plan → sees the one skill that unlocks the most roles → gets a 2-week micro-learning path with curated resources → marks modules complete → her profile auto-updates proficiency.
     AI role: Wiki RAG retrieves authoritative learning resources per skill; Gemini 3.1 Pro sequences them into a time-boxed plan ranked by opportunity unlock.
     Outcome: Maya knows the single highest-leverage skill to build and has a concrete plan to build it before applying.
  8. Submit post-placement reflection
     Trigger: Maya's co-op term ends and the system prompts a structured reflection.
     Flow: She opens the reflection form → rates skills she actually used → describes a key project → the system extracts new competencies demonstrated → her profile is enriched for the next cycle.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro extracts newly-demonstrated competencies from Maya's free-text reflection and proposes profile updates.
     Outcome: Maya's next co-op search starts from a stronger, evidence-backed profile, compounding her readiness over time.
  9. Compare against cohort readiness
     Trigger: Maya wants to know how prepared she is relative to peers.
     Flow: She opens readiness benchmark → sees her percentile on profile completeness and competency breadth → views anonymized cohort distribution → sees which skills are common vs. differentiating in her track.
     AI role: Embeddings cluster cohort competency profiles to position Maya and surface differentiating skills.
     Outcome: Maya gains realistic, non-toxic perspective on where she stands and what makes her stand out.
  10. Request faculty coordinator review
     Trigger: Maya's top matches stay below a confidence threshold after two weeks.
     Flow: System flags her for coordinator review → she requests a meeting → coordinator sees her profile, match history, and gap plan → they co-edit her interest tags and target list.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro generates a coordinator briefing summarizing Maya's blockers and recommended interventions.
     Outcome: Maya gets timely human support before frustration sets in, and the coordinator arrives informed.
  11. Explore stretch and reach roles
     Trigger: Maya filters her feed to see ambitious roles beyond her current fit band.
     Flow: She toggles 'Show reach roles' → amber/red roles appear with explicit 'what it would take' notes → she bookmarks two aspirational roles → they feed into her long-term skill goals.
     AI role: Fit-scoring model surfaces near-miss roles and Claude Opus 4.7 articulates the realistic path to qualifying.
     Outcome: Maya sees aspiration without false hope — a motivating but honest map of where she could grow.
  12. Receive employer interest nudges
     Trigger: A recruiter views or saves Maya's matched profile.
     Flow: She gets a notification that an employer engaged → sees which role and what they likely valued → gets a suggested action (apply now, send note) → acts in one tap.
     AI role: Gemini 3.1 Pro interprets employer engagement signals and recommends the highest-value next action.
     Outcome: Maya capitalizes on warm employer interest she'd otherwise never have known about.

KEY SCREENS (9) - every screen is a real view, not a placeholder:
  1. Onboarding skills intake - purpose: Convert Maya's resume and transcript into a verified, structured competency profile with minimal manual entry.
     Primary element: Card-by-card skill confirmation flow with auto-extracted chips and a 4-level proficiency slider.
     Motion character: Chips fly in from the parsed document, settle into place; the completeness ring fills with a satisfying spring as each skill is confirmed.
  2. Match feed with fit scores - purpose: Present a ranked, scannable set of co-op roles sorted by predicted placement fit.
     Primary element: Vertical list of role cards each anchored by a large color-banded fit score and 3 matched-skill tags.
     Motion character: Cards stagger-assemble top-down as scores resolve from a shimmering placeholder to a crisp number, conveying 'computation finished.'
  3. Match detail with rationale - purpose: Explain the fit score in plain language and visualize the competency overlap and gaps.
     Primary element: Competency-match radar chart paired with a 3-bullet AI rationale and an 'unlock' callout.
     Motion character: Radar polygon draws itself edge by edge; gap segments pulse amber once to draw the eye, then settle.
  4. Application tracker board - purpose: Give Maya a single calm Kanban view of every application's status.
     Primary element: Four-column board (Applied / Viewed / Interviewing / Offer) with auto-moving cards and time-in-stage badges.
     Motion character: Cards glide between columns with a smooth ease when status changes; stale cards gently breathe to signal attention.
  5. Resume tailoring workspace - purpose: Let Maya review and accept AI-suggested resume and cover-letter edits before applying.
     Primary element: Split view: original on left, tracked-change suggestions on right, accept/reject per change.
     Motion character: Accepted changes morph smoothly into the canonical text; the relevance meter ticks upward with each acceptance.
  6. Interview scheduler - purpose: Resolve interview timing against Maya's class calendar in two taps.
     Primary element: Slot grid overlaid with her existing calendar blocks, conflict-free slots highlighted.
     Motion character: Conflicting slots dim and recede; the chosen slot expands and locks with a confirming check pulse.
  7. Skill-gap prep plan - purpose: Show the single highest-leverage skill and a time-boxed path to build it.
     Primary element: Hero 'unlock' stat ('+5 roles') above a sequenced 2-week module checklist with progress.
     Motion character: The unlock number counts up; completing a module fills a segment of the path and re-computes the unlock total live.
  8. Cohort readiness benchmark - purpose: Position Maya against anonymized peers without inducing toxic comparison.
     Primary element: Distribution curve with Maya's marker and a panel of differentiating skills.
     Motion character: Maya's marker slides into position along the curve with a gentle settle; differentiating skills fade in sequentially.
  9. Placement confirmation - purpose: Celebrate and formalize an accepted co-op offer and seed the reflection cycle.
     Primary element: Confirmation hero with employer, role, term, and a 'what you'll grow' competency forecast.
     Motion character: A restrained confetti burst, then the screen transitions to a forward-looking growth forecast — celebratory but grounded.

AI CAPABILITIES (8) - every one wires to a real /api/ai/* endpoint via the multi-provider fallback helper:
  1. Skill-to-role fit scoring
     User action: Completes profile or opens the match feed
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Maya's verified competency profile (skills + proficiency), role required-competency specs, historical placement outcomes for similar student profiles
     Output: A 0–100 placement-fit score per role plus a green/amber/red band and ranked ordering
     User benefit: Maya focuses on roles she can realistically land instead of guessing across hundreds of postings
  2. Match rationale generation
     User action: Opens a role's match detail
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: The numeric fit score, the specific overlapping and missing competencies, the role description
     Output: A 3-bullet, encouraging plain-language explanation of why she fits and what would raise the score
     User benefit: The black box opens — Maya trusts the score because she understands its reasoning
  3. Opportunity-unlock detector (HEADLINE AHA)
     User action: Views her match feed after profile completion
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Maya's current competencies, the full open-role corpus, marginal fit-score deltas if each missing skill were added
     Output: The single skill that would push the most additional roles into a strong-fit band, with the exact count and which roles
     User benefit: Maya sees the one highest-leverage move that multiplies her opportunity set — clarity replaces overwhelm
  4. Resume tailoring assistant
     User action: Clicks Apply on a role
     Model: Claude Opus 4.7
     Input: Maya's base resume, her verified competencies, the target role's required competencies and language
     Output: A role-tailored resume variant and cover letter as accept/reject tracked suggestions
     User benefit: Genuinely tailored applications in minutes, with the right strengths foregrounded
  5. Skill-gap learning sequencing
     User action: Opens the skill-gap prep plan
     Model: Wiki RAG
     Input: The target skill, authoritative learning resources retrieved from a curated knowledge base, a 2-week time budget
     Output: An ordered micro-learning path with vetted resources and estimated effort per module
     User benefit: Maya gets a credible, time-boxed plan instead of a Google rabbit hole
  6. Competency extraction from documents
     User action: Uploads resume / connects transcript / submits reflection
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Resume text, transcript course list, free-text post-placement reflection
     Output: A structured set of competencies with inferred proficiency levels mapped to the taxonomy
     User benefit: Maya's profile builds itself from evidence she already has, no tedious manual entry
  7. Cohort positioning via embeddings
     User action: Opens the readiness benchmark
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: Embedded competency vectors for Maya and the anonymized cohort
     Output: Maya's percentile position and a list of skills that differentiate her within her track
     User benefit: Realistic, motivating self-awareness without raw, demoralizing comparison
  8. Pipeline health summarization
     User action: Opens the application tracker board
     Model: Gemini 3.1 Pro
     Input: All application statuses, time-in-stage, employer engagement signals
     Output: A plain-language health summary plus prioritized follow-up nudges
     User benefit: Maya knows where to put energy next without manually tracking anything

VISUAL DIRECTION:
  Aesthetic keywords: trustworthy collegiate data-forward — warm Northeastern-adjacent reds and deep navy, generous whitespace, confident sans-serif, optimistic but never childish; reads like a well-designed career-services product, not a flashy startup
  Hero treatment: The match feed is the hero surface: a clean vertical column of role cards where the fit score is the single dominant element — large, color-banded, immediately scannable. The opportunity-unlock banner is the emotional centerpiece, treated with a distinct accent panel and an animated count-up that turns abstract opportunity into a concrete, exciting number.
  Motion character: Purposeful and confidence-building, never decorative. Scores count up to feel earned. Cards stagger-assemble to signal 'computation finished and curated for you.' Transitions are smooth eases with occasional gentle springs on positive moments (completeness, unlock). Stale or gap states use soft pulses rather than alarming color.
  Image generation prompts (the prototype should call /api/ai/gemini-image at runtime with these - the runner reads the result and renders it as a hero/empty-state/illustration):
    1. Imagen: a warm, optimistic flat-illustration of a diverse Northeastern student at a laptop with abstract skill-node connections radiating outward, navy and crimson palette, used on the onboarding intake hero
    2. Imagen: an abstract competency-constellation graphic — interconnected glowing nodes forming a profile shape — for the empty-state of the match feed before computation
    3. Imagen: subtle textured 'unlock' badge iconography (a key dissolving into multiplying role-card silhouettes) for the headline opportunity callout
    4. Imagen: a calm, editorial placement-confirmation illustration showing a student stepping onto a path of milestone markers, celebratory yet grounded, for the offer-accepted screen
    5. Imagen: a light geometric background pattern of soft hexagonal skill tiles for section dividers, low-contrast so it never competes with data

INTERACTION CHOREOGRAPHY (10 beats) - the step-by-step script for the HEADLINE aha interaction; honor the timing_ms values where given:
  1. Maya confirms the final skill on her intake and the completeness ring hits 100%.
     System: A subtle 'Building your matches…' state appears and the feed begins to compute.
     Motion/feedback: Completeness ring snaps full with a spring; a soft progress shimmer replaces the feed. (600ms)
  2. Maya waits, watching the feed area.
     System: Fit-scoring runs across all open roles; placeholder cards shimmer.
     Motion/feedback: Skeleton cards pulse with a left-to-right shimmer to signal active computation. (900ms)
  3. Maya sees the first cards resolve.
     System: Cards stagger-assemble top-down, each fit score counting up to its final value.
     Motion/feedback: Each score ticks from 0 to its value in ~400ms with a color band fading from gray to green/amber/red. (1200ms)
  4. Maya registers that her top three are all green-band.
     System: Top matched-skill tags appear under each top card.
     Motion/feedback: Tags fade in sequentially with a 60ms stagger. (500ms)
  5. Maya scrolls slightly and notices a distinct highlighted banner.
     System: The opportunity-unlock callout slides in: 'Add Python basics → unlocks 5 more roles.'
     Motion/feedback: Banner slides down from the feed top with a gentle bounce and an accent glow. (450ms)
  6. Maya taps the unlock banner.
     System: The five roles that would become strong-fit pulse and float to a preview strip.
     Motion/feedback: Five target cards briefly elevate and outline, then gather into a horizontal preview. (700ms)
  7. Maya hovers over one previewed role.
     System: A mini before/after shows its score jumping (e.g., 62 → 81) if Python were added.
     Motion/feedback: A small score gauge animates from current to projected with an amber-to-green sweep. (550ms)
  8. Maya clicks 'See how to add Python.'
     System: The skill-gap prep plan opens with a 2-week sequenced micro-path.
     Motion/feedback: Screen cross-fades; the unlock stat '+5 roles' counts up as the hero. (600ms)
  9. Maya marks the first module 'in progress.'
     System: Her projected proficiency updates and the unlock total re-computes live.
     Motion/feedback: A path segment fills; the '+5' briefly flickers as it recalculates and resettles. (500ms)
  10. Maya navigates back to the feed.
     System: The previously locked roles now show a 'pending Python' badge, framing them as soon-reachable.
     Motion/feedback: Badges fade in on the relevant cards; the feed feels visibly larger and more open. (450ms)

SUCCESS CRITERIA (Stage 5 audits the prototype against each of these):
  - 90% of new users complete a competency profile and reach a populated, explained match feed within 10 minutes
  - Every match score is accompanied by a plain-language rationale users rate as understandable in ≥85% of cases
  - The opportunity-unlock feature is engaged by ≥60% of users within their first session
  - Median time from intent-to-apply to submitted tailored application falls below 5 minutes
  - Users report reduced co-op-search anxiety (pre/post self-rating improves by ≥1.5 points on a 5-point scale)
  - Returning students start their next cycle with at least 3 newly-extracted competencies from reflection
  - All core flows pass WCAG AA, including keyboard navigation of the match feed and tracker board

HARD CONSTRAINTS:
  Brand: Northeastern University co-op program brand alignment — collegiate, trustworthy, accessible; crimson/navy palette permitted but must not impersonate official university crests without approval
  Platform: web
  Accessibility: WCAG AA
  Other:
    - Student data handling must respect FERPA expectations; no exposure of GPA or identifiable peer data in benchmarks (anonymized aggregates only)
    - AI rationale must be encouraging and non-deterministic about outcomes — never guarantee placement
    - All AI capabilities require multi-provider fallback (Gemini primary, Claude secondary) with graceful degradation
    - Match scores must always be explainable; no unexplained numeric rankings shown to students

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an expert career advisor AI. Parse the provided resume text and transcript courses into a structured array of competencies. Map them to standard industry skills and infer a proficiency level (Aware, Practicing, Proficient, Expert) based on the evidence.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Extract competencies from this resume: {{resume_text}} and transcript: {{transcript_text}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a placement-fit prediction model. Compare a student's verified competency profile against a corpus of open co-op roles. Calculate a 0-100 fit score based on competency overlap, proficiency depth, and historical placement patterns.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Score fit for student {{student_profile}} against roles {{open_roles_corpus}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an opportunity-maximization engine. Analyze a student's missing competencies across all roles. Identify the single skill that, if added at a 'Practicing' level, would push the highest number of roles from amber/red into the green strong-fit band.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Find the highest-leverage missing skill for student {{student_profile}} across roles {{open_roles_corpus}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an encouraging, transparent career coach. Explain a numeric fit score in 3 plain-language bullets. Highlight the strongest overlapping competencies, identify the specific gaps, and explain what it would take to close them. Never guarantee placement.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Generate rationale for a {{fit_score}}% match between student {{student_profile}} and role {{role_details}}.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are a curriculum designer. Given a target skill and a 2-week time budget, retrieve authoritative learning resources and sequence them into an ordered micro-learning path with estimated effort per module.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Create a 2-week prep plan to learn {{unlock_skill}} to a 'Practicing' level.

ai_flows.system_prompt_outline: You are an expert resume writer. Rewrite the student's base resume bullets to emphasize the competencies required by the target role. Draft a tailored cover letter anchored to the role's requirements and the student's verified strengths. Output as tracked changes.
ai_flows.user_message_template: Tailor resume {{base_resume}} and draft cover letter for role {{role_details}}.

critique.summary: The prototype successfully implements the visual design and interaction patterns, but fails to wire the AI flows to real endpoints, relying entirely on mock timeouts. The corrected code wires all 5 AI flows to the multi-provider fallback helper and adds missing accessibility attributes.

Add aria-labels to buttons and inputs.
